A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AE-SVC and (SS)2D research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments on four datasets, including main-text and appendix performance curves and cosine-similarity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original retrieval experiments and adds network-depth and constraint-placement ablations and further baseline comparisons in Appendices A.7–A.9.

M1.justification: The AE-SVC constraints, reconstruction objective, and nested similarity-distillation procedure remain unchanged in Section 3. The newly documented three-layer architecture and experimental variants do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate InShop, SOP, Pittsburgh30K, and TokyoVal for product retrieval and place recognition. Additional backbone combinations and the mentioned held-out training split do not introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Appendix A.9/Figure 9 adds PCA Whitening and TLDR to direct AE-SVC comparisons alongside PCA and VAE across all four datasets. These materially broaden the comparator set beyond v1's PCA comparisons for AE-SVC and VAE/SSD comparisons for (SS)2D.

E3.justification: Added experiments vary network depth and constraint location, while Figures 5 and 7 expand backbone–dataset combinations and include smaller embedding sizes. Figure 4 changes the displayed ViT/DINOv2-Large dimension range from 1024 to 768. Appendix A.9 mentions held-out training only in its heading, leaving that split's implementation unresolved.

E4.justification: New Tables 1–2 systematically test encoder/decoder depth and whether constraints act at the representation or successive decoder layers. These address two design questions without corresponding ablations in v1; the existing cosine-distribution analysis remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 4, 5, and 7 revise curves and add configuration results, including changes within panels moved between the main text and appendix. Section 5.2 changes DINOv2-Large's reported Pittsburgh30K improvement from 5% to 2%. Tables 1–2 and Figure 9 add substantial findings; for example, Table 1 reports 384-dimensional mAP@4 of 0.568 for three layers versus 0.200 for ten.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, Gaussian assumptions, cosine-variance approximation and derivation in Section 4, and orthogonal-transformation and scale-invariance proofs in Appendices A.1–A.2 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about unsupervised embedding improvement and adaptive dimensionality reduction remain unchanged. The conclusion's 16% becomes 15.5%, matching the average already reported in v1; the abstract retains its original claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.7 newly interprets deeper-network deterioration as diminishing returns and possible overfitting. Appendices A.8–A.9 argue for representation-level constraints over decoder-level application. Section 5.3's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies that all experiments use three-layer encoders/decoders and documents the ablation configurations. It removes v1's supplementary-code availability statements, including references to dataloaders and reproduction instructions. The PDFs do not establish whether the actual code resource was withdrawn.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for PCA Whitening and TLDR and explicitly distinguishes AE-SVC from TLDR by losses and constraint placement in Appendix A.9. Additional citations expand Section 2 modestly, while its structure and broad novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. Changes are localized to introduction wording, results descriptions, reproducibility statements, three added appendix subsections, acknowledgments, and publication/author text.

P2.justification: Figures 4, 5, and 7 are redrawn; Figures 5 and 7 each expand from two to four panels, with some configurations moving between them. New Tables 1–2 and Figure 9 substantially extend the empirical displays. The ICLR template also changes headings, headers, and page flow.

improvement.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 9 strengthen the empirical case by testing previously unsupported architectural choices and adding relevant whitening and TLDR comparisons. These gains are moderated by removal of code-release information and the unspecified held-out training protocol in Appendix A.9. The added evidence supports a limited overall improvement, without establishing performance gains under unchanged settings.
